modules.title: The Math That Powers Magic

lessons.title: Why Randomness is Everything: Probability & Distributions for Generative AI
key_formulas: Gaussian PDF: p(x) = (1/√(2πσ²)) exp(-(x-μ)²/2σ²)
KL Divergence: D_KL(P||Q) = Σ P(x) log(P(x)/Q(x))
Bayes' Theorem: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A) / P(B)
Reparameterization trick: z = μ + σ·ε where ε ~ N(0,1)
key_code_demos: Animate sampling from Gaussian vs multimodal distributions — watch dots materialize from the density curve
Animate KL divergence as two Gaussians drift apart — divergence meter updates live
Interactive: drag μ and σ sliders, watch the bell curve reshape in real time
learning_objectives: Explain Gaussian distributions, KL divergence, and conditional probability using visual intuition
Interpret probability density functions and what 'sampling from a distribution' means geometrically
Connect Bayes' theorem to how generative models reason about data

lessons.title: The Convolution Superpower: CNNs That See at Every Scale
key_formulas: 2D Convolution: (I * K)[i,j] = ΣΣ I[i+m, j+n] · K[m,n]
Residual connection: y = F(x, W) + x
Group Normalization: x̂ = (x - μ_g) / √(σ²_g + ε) per group g
key_code_demos: Animate a 3×3 filter sliding over an image — feature map pixels light up as kernel sweeps
Layer-by-layer activation map viewer: shallow = Gabor-like edges, deep = object parts
Training loss curves with/without residual connections — show gradient flow collapse without them
learning_objectives: Illustrate how convolution filters detect edges, textures, and high-level patterns layer by layer
Explain spatial downsampling, residual connections, and GroupNorm in modern CNN blocks
Compare feature map resolutions — show how shallow layers see edges, deep layers see semantics

lessons.title: Training Machines to Learn: Backprop & Optimization Demystified
key_formulas: Chain rule: ∂L/∂w = ∂L/∂y · ∂y/∂w
Adam update: m_t = β₁m_{t-1} + (1-β₁)g_t; v_t = β₂v_{t-1} + (1-β₂)g²_t; w -= α·m̂_t/√(v̂_t)+ε
Gradient clipping: g̃ = g · min(1, threshold/||g||)
key_code_demos: Full training loop from scratch: DataLoader → forward → loss → .backward() → optimizer.step()
Live per-layer gradient norm plot — watch gradients vanish in deep networks without normalization
Adam vs SGD+momentum race on MNIST: side-by-side loss curves updating in real time
learning_objectives: Implement a manual forward + backward pass in PyTorch to solidify gradient intuition
Compare Adam, SGD, and cosine LR scheduling using live loss curve visualization
Diagnose vanishing/exploding gradients and apply gradient clipping and normalization fixes

modules.description: Lock in the probability, statistics, and CNN intuition that every generative model is secretly built on. Visually-driven — no formula without a picture.

modules.title: Teaching Machines to Create

lessons.title: The Compression Secret: VAEs and the Geometry of Latent Space
key_formulas: ELBO: L = E[log p(x|z)] - D_KL(q(z|x) || p(z))
Reparameterization: z = μ_φ(x) + σ_φ(x) · ε where ε ~ N(0,I)
Reconstruction loss: -E_q[log p_θ(x|z)]
β-VAE objective: L_β = reconstruction_loss + β · D_KL
key_code_demos: Train VAE on MNIST — animate latent space 2D scatter plot forming digit clusters epoch by epoch
Latent interpolation: smoothly morph digit '3' into '8' by walking through z-space
Show β-VAE effect: β=1 (blurry but structured) vs β=10 (sharp disentanglement)
learning_objectives: Explain the encoder-decoder structure and the ELBO objective with visual intuition
Describe why the reparameterization trick enables backprop through stochastic sampling
Visualize and interpret a trained VAE's latent space — interpolation paths, clusters, and disentanglement

lessons.title: The Adversarial Game: GANs Learning to Hallucinate Reality
key_formulas: GAN minimax: min_G max_D E[log D(x)] + E[log(1 - D(G(z)))]
Wasserstein distance: W(P_r, P_g) = inf_{γ~Π(P_r,P_g)} E[(x,y)~γ][||x-y||]
WGAN-GP penalty: λ · E[(||∇_x̂ D(x̂)||₂ - 1)²]
key_code_demos: Animate discriminator decision boundary evolving as generator improves over training iterations
Mode collapse visualization — GAN generating only 2 of 10 MNIST digit classes
Loss curve comparison: vanilla GAN (oscillating/diverging) vs WGAN-GP (smooth descent)
learning_objectives: Explain the generator-discriminator minimax game using game theory intuition
Identify GAN failure modes — mode collapse, training instability — and how WGAN-GP addresses them
Compare VAE vs GAN quality trade-offs and articulate when each is preferable

lessons.title: Time Traveling Networks: How Models Learn Motion & Sequences
key_formulas: Self-attention: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V
Sinusoidal positional encoding: PE(pos, 2i) = sin(pos / 10000^(2i/d_model))
LSTM forget gate: f_t = σ(W_f · [h_{t-1}, x_t] + b_f)
key_code_demos: Animate attention weight matrix across a video sequence — watch frame t attend to frames t-2, t-3
LSTM hidden state activation heatmap on a video frame prediction task
Build a temporal self-attention block and visualize the (T×T) attention matrix as a heatmap
topics_covered: Temporal Modeling & Sequential Data in Deep Learning
learning_objectives: Explain temporal self-attention and how it captures long-range dependencies across frames
Compare RNN/LSTM vs Transformer approaches — and argue why Transformers dominate for video
Apply positional encoding intuition to understand how models know 'when' in a sequence

modules.description: Understand the generative model family tree — VAEs, GANs, and temporal networks — that set the stage for diffusion. Build latent space intuition and learn why sequence modeling is the key to video.

modules.title: Noise to Masterpiece: Diffusion Model Fundamentals

lessons.title: Corrupting to Learn: The Forward Process & Noise Schedules
key_formulas: Forward step: q(x_t|x_{t-1}) = N(x_t; √(1-β_t)x_{t-1}, β_t I)
Closed-form marginal: q(x_t|x_0) = N(x_t; √ᾱ_t x_0, (1-ᾱ_t) I)
Cumulative product: ᾱ_t = Π_{s=1}^{t}(1-β_s)
Cosine schedule: ᾱ_t = cos²(((t/T + s)/(1+s)) · π/2)
key_code_demos: Animate a photo dissolving into pure Gaussian noise across T=1000 steps — frame scrubber control
Side-by-side: linear vs cosine schedule — ᾱ_t curve plotted alongside noisy image at each step
Verify closed-form marginal matches step-by-step noising — overlay histograms at t=500, t=999
learning_objectives: Explain the DDPM forward process q(x_t|x_0) and derive the closed-form marginal that makes training tractable
Visualize how linear vs cosine noise schedules degrade images differently across 1000 timesteps
Distinguish what the model actually learns to predict — noise ε vs original image x_0

lessons.title: Reversing Chaos: Training the Denoising Network from Scratch
key_formulas: Training objective: L_simple = E_{x_0,ε,t}[||ε - ε_θ(x_t, t)||²]
Reverse process: p_θ(x_{t-1}|x_t) = N(x_{t-1}; μ_θ(x_t,t), Σ_θ(x_t,t))
Predicted mean: μ_θ(x_t,t) = (1/√α_t)(x_t - (β_t/√(1-ᾱ_t)) ε_θ(x_t,t))
key_code_demos: Full DDPM training loop on MNIST — loss curve + sample grid updating every 500 steps
Animate the reverse denoising: T=1000→0 showing a digit emerging from static noise
Noise vs x_0 prediction comparison: train both, overlay loss curves and final sample quality
learning_objectives: Implement the DDPM training objective and explain noise prediction vs x_0 prediction equivalence
Build a U-Net denoiser with timestep conditioning in PyTorch from scratch
Train a DDPM on MNIST and visualize the full denoising trajectory from pure noise to digit

lessons.title: Speed Without Sacrifice: DDIM, Score Matching & Smarter Sampling
key_formulas: DDIM update: x_{t-1} = √ᾱ_{t-1}·f_θ(x_t) + √(1-ᾱ_{t-1}-σ_t²)·ε_θ(x_t,t) + σ_t·ε
Score function: ∇_x log p_t(x) ≈ -ε_θ(x_t,t) / √(1-ᾱ_t)
Classifier-free guidance: ε̃ = ε_θ(x_t,∅) + w·(ε_θ(x_t,c) - ε_θ(x_t,∅))
key_code_demos: Generate the same image: DDPM (1000 steps, ~60s) vs DDIM (50 steps, ~3s) — quality comparison grid
Score function vector field visualization — arrows pointing toward data manifold
Guidance scale sweep w=1→15: diversity-vs-fidelity slider, watch images sharpen and mode-collapse
topics_covered: Improved Sampling: DDIM, Score Matching & Noise Schedules
learning_objectives: Explain DDIM's deterministic non-Markovian sampling and why it enables 10–50× speedup
Connect the denoising network to the score function ∇_x log p_t(x) via Tweedie's formula
Compare DDPM, DDIM, and DPM-Solver on the speed vs quality frontier

modules.description: Understand how DDPM systematically destroys images and learns to reverse the process — then build and train one from scratch. Unlock faster sampling with DDIM and score matching.

modules.title: The Architecture of Dreams: Latent Diffusion & U-Net Mastery

lessons.title: Compress Then Create: How Latent Diffusion Breaks the Compute Wall
key_formulas: Perceptual loss: L_perc = ||φ(x) - φ(x̂)||² where φ extracts VGG features
LDM objective: L_LDM = E_{z~E(x), ε, t}[||ε - ε_θ(z_t, t)||²]
Compression ratio: z ∈ ℝ^{H/f × W/f × c} from x ∈ ℝ^{H×W×3} with f typically 8
key_code_demos: Encode an image with VQ-VAE at f=8 — animate reconstruction quality vs compression ratio
Pixel diffusion vs latent diffusion: same FID at 64× less memory — bar chart + sample grid
Latent arithmetic: encode two images, interpolate z, decode — watch smooth semantic blending
learning_objectives: Explain why pixel-space diffusion is compute-prohibitive and how LDMs solve it via perceptual compression
Describe the two-stage LDM pipeline: train a VQ-VAE encoder, then diffuse in its latent space
Compare LDM vs pixel diffusion on FID, memory footprint, and generation speed

lessons.title: The U-Net Inside Every Diffusion Model: Skip Connections, Attention & Conditioning
key_formulas: Timestep conditioning: h = h + MLP(t_emb) then GroupNorm + SiLU activation
Cross-attention: Attention(Q=h_img, K=c_text, V=c_text) for text-guided generation
AdaGroupNorm: ĥ = (1 + γ(t))·(h - μ)/σ + β(t) where γ,β learned from timestep
key_code_demos: Animated U-Net diagram: feature maps flowing down encoder, up decoder, skip connections highlighted
Cross-attention heatmaps: 'a red car' — show 'red' attending to car pixels, 'car' to shape regions
PyTorch implementation: ResBlock + SelfAttn + CrossAttn + Upsample — full U-Net block stack
learning_objectives: Trace the U-Net encoder-decoder path and explain why skip connections preserve spatial detail
Implement self-attention and cross-attention blocks inside U-Net residual layers
Explain timestep and text conditioning injection via AdaGN and cross-attention

lessons.title: Conditioning the Dream: Text Control & Classifier-Free Guidance
key_formulas: CFG: ε̃_θ(x_t,c) = ε_θ(x_t,∅) + w·(ε_θ(x_t,c) - ε_θ(x_t,∅))
CLIP similarity: cos(E_I(x), E_T(c)) where E_I, E_T are image/text towers
Dropout training: randomly set c → ∅ with p=0.1 to learn unconditional score
key_code_demos: Guidance scale sweep w=1→15 — grid showing diversity collapse into hyper-sharp samples
Text-conditional generation on CIFAR-10: prompt 'airplane', 'dog', 'ship' — see class emerge
CLIP similarity score meter updating live as guidance scale changes
learning_objectives: Implement classifier-free guidance for conditional image generation from scratch
Integrate a CLIP text encoder to condition the U-Net on text prompts via cross-attention
Evaluate conditional generation quality using FID and CLIP similarity scores

modules.description: Discover how Stable Diffusion compresses images into latent space before diffusing — and master the attention-augmented U-Net that makes high-resolution generation tractable.

modules.title: Lights, Camera, Diffusion: Building Video Generation from Scratch

lessons.title: Frames That Flow: Temporal Attention for Motion Consistency
key_formulas: Temporal attention: Attn_T(Q,K,V) where Q,K,V reshape across T frames per spatial location
Factorized: Attn_ST(h) = Attn_S(Attn_T(h)) — temporal first, then spatial
Video DDPM joint forward: q(x^{1:T}_t | x^{1:T}_0) = Π_i q(x^i_t | x^i_0) shared ᾱ_t
key_code_demos: Temporal attention heatmap: frame t attending to frames t-1, t-2 — motion consistency visualized
FVD vs FLOPs scatter plot: factorized vs full 3D attention Pareto frontier
Animate 16-frame video being noised: all frames degrade together with shared noise schedule
topics_covered: Video Diffusion Models: Temporal Attention & 3D Architectures
learning_objectives: Explain how temporal self-attention enables frames to communicate across time for motion coherence
Compare factorized spatial-temporal attention vs full 3D attention on compute and quality trade-offs
Describe how Video Diffusion Models extend DDPM to video with joint noise across all frames

lessons.title: Into the Third Dimension: 3D U-Net & Spatiotemporal Convolutions
key_formulas: 3D convolution: (V * K)[t,h,w] = ΣΣΣ V[t+τ, h+i, w+j] · K[τ,i,j]
Pseudo-3D: P3D(x) = Conv1D_T(Conv2D_S(x)) — decomposed for 4× efficiency
Temporal inflation init: K_3D[τ,i,j] = K_2D[i,j]/T if τ=T//2, else 0
key_code_demos: Animated 3D convolution kernel sweeping through a (T, H, W) video volume
Parameter count comparison: full 3D conv vs pseudo-3D for same receptive field
Inflate a pretrained 2D MNIST U-Net to 3D — watch fine-tuning converge in 10% the epochs
topics_covered: Video Diffusion Models: Temporal Attention & 3D Architectures
learning_objectives: Implement pseudo-3D convolutions (2D spatial + 1D temporal) as an efficient alternative to full 3D
Explain how inflated 3D convolutions extend a pretrained image U-Net to video with minimal new parameters
Design a 3D U-Net that processes video clips as (T, H, W, C) spatiotemporal volumes

lessons.title: Your First Video Diffusion Model: Architecture to Training Loop
key_formulas: Video training loss: L = E_{x_0,ε,t}[||ε - ε_θ(x_t, t)||²] where x_0 ∈ ℝ^{T×C×H×W}
Temporal consistency reg: λ·||ε_θ(x_t,t)^{i+1} - ε_θ(x_t,t)^i||² added to loss
Frame noise injection: ε^i ~ N(0,I) independently per frame, shared t across clip
key_code_demos: VideoUNet class in PyTorch: 3DResBlock → TemporalAttn → SpatialAttn layer assembly
Training loop with video batches: sample clips → add noise → predict → backprop
Generated video samples during training: watch inter-frame flickering reduce over epochs
topics_covered: Building a Video Generation Pipeline from Scratch
learning_objectives: Assemble a complete video U-Net: 3D ResBlocks, temporal attention, spatial attention
Implement the video diffusion training loop with (B, T, C, H, W) tensor batches
Train on a short video dataset and debug temporal flickering using consistency regularization

lessons.title: Ship It: The Complete Text-to-Video Generation Pipeline
key_formulas: FVD: Fréchet distance in I3D feature space between real and generated video distributions
Video DDIM: same update rule applied per-frame with shared deterministic schedule
Text injection: CrossAttn(Q=video_feat, K=CLIP(prompt), V=CLIP(prompt)) per U-Net block
key_code_demos: End-to-end pipeline: text prompt → CLIP encode → DDIM 50-step video sample → decode → save .mp4
Temporal attention ablation: generation with vs without temporal attn — flicker comparison side-by-side
Generate 'a bouncing ball', 'ocean waves', 'rotating cube' — visualize all three .mp4 outputs
topics_covered: Building a Video Generation Pipeline from Scratch
learning_objectives: Integrate CLIP text conditioning into the video U-Net for text-to-video generation
Implement DDIM sampling over video frames for fast generation (50 steps vs 1000)
Evaluate generated videos with FVD (Fréchet Video Distance) and build an end-to-end generation script

modules.description: Extend everything you've built to video — temporal attention, 3D convolutions, and a full end-to-end text-to-video pipeline. Final project: a working video generation model you designed.

course_title: Diffusion Models to Video Generation: Build It from Scratch
course_description: A visual-first, hands-on journey from probability foundations through cutting-edge video diffusion models. By the end, you'll have built a working text-to-video generation pipeline from scratch — understanding every equation, every architectural choice, and every line of code.
